extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for advancing the state-of-the-art in object recognition by placing the question of object recognition in the context of the broader question of scene understanding. It contains photos of complex everyday scenes containing common objects in their natural context, labeled using per-instance segmentations to aid in precise object localization.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.citeAs: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár. Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context. arXiv:1405.0312v3. 2015.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were harvested from Flickr using queries for pairs of objects or scene/object category pairs to find non-iconic images containing contextual relationships. At most 5 photos were downloaded from a single photographer within a short time window. An AMT filtering task was used to remove invalid or iconic images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Segmentations were not collected for 11 categories (hat, shoe, eyeglasses, mirror, window, door, street sign, plate, desk, blender, hair brush) due to difficulty, ambiguity, or instance count issues. Instances beyond 10-15 per category in an image were marked as 'crowds' and not individually segmented.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Flickr photos uploaded by amateur photographers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Near-duplicate images were removed, and images were grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize duplicates across splits.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An AMT filtering task was used to remove invalid or iconic images from the candidate set retrieved from Flickr.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A pipeline involving: 1) Category Labeling (hierarchical approach, dragging icons onto instances), 2) Instance Spotting (clicking crosses on instances), 3) Instance Segmentation (drawing polygons using a modified OpenSurfaces UI), 4) Segmentation Verification (judging quality), 5) Crowd Labeling (painting pixels for >10 instances).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Union of 8 AMT workers achieved greater recall than expert workers. Over 99% of object categories are detected given 8 annotators. Workers with high precision completed the most jobs; jobs from low precision workers were rejected. Segmentations were verified by 3-5 workers; those with less than 4/5 favorable votes were discarded.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 8 workers for category labeling and instance spotting; 1 worker for instance segmentation (verified by 3-5 workers).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Split into two parts: 2014 release and 2015 release. The dataset will evolve and grow over time; up to date information is available online.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Dataset focuses on non-iconic images and 'thing' categories rather than 'stuff'. Images sourced from Flickr (amateur photographers).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Only 'thing' categories are labeled, not 'stuff'. 11 categories omitted from segmentation. Dense crowds of objects are not individually segmented. Ambiguity in category presence exists.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Object recognition, scene understanding, detecting non-iconic views, contextual reasoning, precise 2D localization, bounding box detection, segmentation detection.
